en: Translated by the śramaṇa Amoghavajra, Tripitaka Master of the Seven Koṭis of Independent Teachings.
This is the summary of the seals (*mudrā*) of the twenty-five great maṇḍalas. With the two ring fingers of both hands...
The little fingers are interlaced within;
the two middle fingers are held upright and pressed against each other.
Place the two index fingers upon the first joints of the two middle fingers; then,
with the two thumbs, press the middle joints of the ring fingers of both hands.
If there is an invocation,
move the two index fingers back and forth.
The Buddha said that this mantra and mudrā can extinguish all grave offenses, including the ten evil deeds and the five heinous crimes.
One accomplishes all the merits of pure dharmas (*śukladharma*).
In performing this rite, one makes no distinction between laypeople and monastics;
even for laypeople who drink alcohol, eat meat, and have wives and children, there is no distinction made regarding purity or impurity.
Relying solely upon my Dharma, there is nothing that cannot be accomplished.
First is the ritual for the altar;
second is the ritual for recitation.
The third is the method for accomplishing proofs;
the fourth is the extensive explanation of the methods of mastery;
the fifth is the attainment of great supernormal powers by the devas.
1. Chapter One: The Ritual of the Mandala. The Buddha said: "If one seeks accomplishment, one should first perform the ritual of the mandala, which differs from those of the various sections.
One should dig the ground to create the mandala and smear it with fragrant mud. This is how it is established."
However, using a single new and clean vessel that has never been used,
one should make offerings according to one's ability before an image of the Buddha on the night of the fifteenth day of the month.
Burn agalloch incense and pure water; first,
one should settle the mind and remain free from all discursive thought,
and then, forming the mudrā, recite the mantra.
Recite the mantra over the mirror one hundred and eight times.
Place the mirror in a pouch or casket and always carry it with you.
When you wish to recite, simply take this mirror.
Place it before you, form the mudrā, and recite the mantra;
by using a mirror as the altar, one will immediately attain accomplishment.
Second, the Method of Recitation: The Buddha said that those who wish to uphold this dharma should do so on the night of the fifteenth day.
Having bathed with pure water and put on clean garments,
one sits in the half-lotus posture facing east,
with a mirror placed before oneself.
According to one's capacity, using incense, flowers, pure water, and other such items,
one should first settle the mind and sever all discursive thoughts;
thereafter, one should form the mudrā and seal it upon the heart.
Recite this mantra one hundred and eight times.
When holding this mantra,
it can cause those with short lifespans to attain long lives.
Even the kāmalā disease can be cured,
let alone other ailments;
it is impossible that it would not be eliminated and healed.
On the first, eighth, fourteenth, fifteenth, eighteenth, and twenty-third days of each month.
On the twenty-fourth, twenty-eighth, twenty-ninth, and thirtieth days—
thus for ten days— at dawn each morning.
Rinse the mouth with clear water while facing east.
Recite this mantra one hundred and eight times before consuming food or drink.
Even if one has a wife and children and does not abstain from pungent foods or meat, one will still achieve the desired results.

3. The Method for Accomplishing Manifestation (Siddhi). Regarding the method for accomplishing manifestation, on the eighteenth day of each month, one should perform recitation while visualizing the object and forming mudrās.
With the exception of the ten days of fasting (upoṣadha), it is not necessary to face a mirror or form mudrās.
However, on an ordinary morning before the meat has been seasoned with salt,
once one has recited and maintained this dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times,
one shall not be interrupted for forty-nine days.
Whenever there are matters of good or evil, auspiciousness or calamity,
the Bodhisattva Cundī shall cause the two holy ones to follow that person;
for all matters concerning their wholesome or unwholesome thoughts, one should recite the mantra seven times.
When washing one's face and sprinkling water on the body, one should cultivate the thought of joy;
this can cause kings, ministers, and elders to give rise to a mind of reverence,
which is like the joy felt when a subject honors its lord.
Just as a father loves his son,
he fulfills whatever the latter desires,
not sparing even his own body or life, so that all things are accomplished.
If there are sentient beings with short lifespans or chronic illnesses,
on the night of the fifteenth day of the month at dawn,
they should burn agalloch incense and recite this mantra one thousand times.
The demons lost their minds and ran about wildly;
foxes, hares, and evil spirits all saw their own forms reflected in the mirror.
When commanded to kill, they would kill; when commanded to release, they would release.
Furthermore, they shall not return again for immeasurable eons to increase their lifespan.
Moreover, if there are those who lack merit and auspicious marks,
seeking office without promotion and oppressed by poverty and suffering;
Recite this mantra every ten days of the lunar cycle;
it can cause one to attain the rank of a Wheel-Turning King (Cakravartin) in the present life,
and whatever official position one seeks shall surely be fulfilled.
If a person wishes to travel or perform any task,
they should first contemplate the Holy One, Cundī,
and mentally recite this mantra seven times in full.
If, while one is engaged in some activity or steadying the body for a brief moment,
the body spontaneously begins to shake,
one should know that one's undertaking will be successfully accomplished and that auspicious blessings will follow.
If the body becomes rigid and stiff while moving forward or backward,
one should know that the objective will not be achieved and that calamities will surely follow.
If one wishes to summon the Four Heavenly Kings, Brahmā, Śakra, the twenty-eight classes of devas, Pāpīyān, and others, [one must proceed with this awareness].
Facing a mirror, form the mudrā with the index fingers moving back and forth.
In a pure place, recite [the mantra] twenty-one times aloud.
O noble and holy Yama, King of the Ghosts, and your retinue!
One must comply with their wishes and dare not advance or retreat;
whatever they command shall be carried out according to their will.
If one wishes to know whether this rite has succeeded or failed:
Recite the mantra according to the ritual procedure seven times in full.
In a dream, one will see Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, flowers, and fruits;
black matter will issue from the mouth, which is then consumed as white matter.
One immediately knows that accomplishment has been achieved.
4. Extensive Explanation of the Dharma of Sovereignty, Part Four: Extensive Explanation of the Dharma of Sovereignty. The Buddha said: "This dhāraṇī possesses great power."
One can move Mount Sumeru and the waters of the great ocean;
one can cause withered wood to sprout flowers and fruit through incantation.
If one constantly recites and maintains this, water cannot drown them and fire cannot burn them.
Poisons, the power of weapons, enemies, and diseases shall all be unable to cause harm.
If one knows that there is a treasure hidden within the earth,
one should bind the mudrā and recite the mantra seven times in full.
Treasures hidden within the earth will spontaneously emerge;
whatever one desires shall be fully obtained.
In the face of military arrays or the perils of bandits, one should form the mudrā and seal one’s finger.
They will all retreat and disperse wherever they may be.
If someone should suddenly die from being harmed by ghosts or spirits,
one should bind the mudrā and recite the mantra seven times.
If one seals the heart with this mudrā, those who have suddenly died or suffer from grave illnesses will immediately be restored to life.
If a residence is unsettled and spirits or ghosts cause calamities, one should recite the mantra over four lumps of earth and place them as talismans; they will then depart.
Furthermore, if there are those whose six relations are in discord and whom others do not love or cherish,
by reciting this mantra according to the Dharma, all they encounter will become harmonious;
upon hearing its name or seeing its form, all will give rise to joy and desire never to abandon it.
Within a fierce fire, by pointing with this mudrā, the fire is immediately extinguished;
by pointing with this mudrā at water, the waves are all stilled.
Whatever aspirations one seeks shall be fulfilled without exception.
How much more so if one can further form mudrās, observe the precepts, and recite according to the ritual;
without changing one's physical body, one shall go to the pure lands of the four directions.
Fifth, one attains great supernormal powers (*ṛddhi*): if one seeks long life or commands the various immortals (*ṛṣi*) to procure their elixirs of immortality, [one shall succeed].
Before an ancient stupa, in deep mountains, or within a pure chamber,
one should establish an altar using a mirror as the basis;
this should be maintained for a full seven days or twenty-one days.
Burn blue lotuses mixed with agallochum incense.
During the first watch of the night, recite the mantra one hundred and eight times and then go to sleep.
Either in a dream you will consume the elixir of the immortals, or you will receive the methods for its collection.
Alternatively, if there are five-colored lights before a mirror, within which are medicinal herbs, one may eat them at will and immediately attain the Way of the Immortals.
All other powers and merits are hundreds of thousands of millions of times greater.
It cannot be fully described.
Regarding the specific methods for Cundī: first, place the index, ring, and little fingers of the left hand within the palm.
With the thumbs, press upon the nails of the index, ring, and little fingers;
do the same with the right hand.
Join the two middle fingers so that their tips touch while reciting the mantra;
this is the mudrā for binding the boundary (sīmābandha). With both hands, left and right...
The middle fingers and ring fingers are interlaced inward;
the two little fingers are held upright,
and the two index fingers touch at their tips.
The Body-Protection Mudrā: With both hands in the añjali gesture, each thumb presses against the middle joint of its respective index finger while reciting the mantra.
The two hands are joined in palms-together.
The two hands point outward with the fingers interlaced;
the thumbs are joined together, pressing upon the middle joints of the index fingers;
the three fingers from the middle finger downward are held straight and upright, joined together.
If you encounter thieves or bandits, wear the seal upon the crown of your head:
first seal the left shoulder, then the right;
seal the heart, then the top of the head, and finally between the eyebrows.
This [mudrā] may not be infringed upon.
It is the Illness-Curing Seal.
The second fingers are the two index fingers, the two middle fingers, and the fourth fingers.
Cross the two ring fingers and the two little fingers inward;
join the four fingers outwardly against one another and place the palms together.
The two thumbs are pressed together at the middle joints of the index fingers;
this is the General Gathering Seal (*saṃgraha-mudrā*).
The left and right ring fingers and little fingers are interlaced within the palms.
The two middle fingers are held upright with their tips joined;
the two index fingers are slightly bent and spread apart;
and the two thumbs press down upon the ring fingers.
When summoning, move the index finger back and forth;
sit as if upon a flower pedestal and recite the mantra seven times.
Apply the seal to both shoulders, the throat, below the eyebrows, and the hairline.
Then, with this same seal at the heart, recite the mantra one hundred and eight times.
This is the Seal for Destroying the Heavenly Māras.
With the four fingers of both hands,
press the thumbs into the palms;
clench the fists tightly— this is it.
In any place where there is fear,
such as the suspicion of malevolent spirits or venomous dragons,
one should immediately form this mudrā and recite the mantra with a wrathful voice.
The Seal for Invoking Ghosts and Spirits:
Press the right middle finger over the thumb to rest upon the altar;
extend the remaining fingers upward so that they resemble fangs.
Slightly bend the index and little fingers and move them back and forth;
recite the mantra seven times.
At the third repetition, all ghosts and spirits will immediately arrive.
The above are the ritual manuals for the seven *koṭi* of individual sections.
Formerly, there was a *vinaya*-master who saw a manuscript containing only the brief titles.
It is stated that there is no distinction made between laypeople and monastics, nor regarding the drinking of alcohol, the eating of meat, or having wives and children;
furthermore, no distinction is made between the pure and the impure.
Misreading the text, they treat it as a spurious work. During the Tianming era, the śramaṇa Liangxiong clarified these errors.
The manuscript with the full titles serves as the original version;
those with abbreviated titles are drafts that have not yet been finalized.
As for the śramaṇa Huili:
The version with the full title printed on the cover has circulated in the world;
in my view, this is incorrect.
I have relied upon Yu’s draft to reach a decision.
The *Hikishō Mondō* and other works cite this ritual manual;
this year, it was compiled at Seiwain in Northern Rokuhara.
Various editions preserved at Chikaku-in in Raku-tō, Enmyō-ji in Kawa-shū,
and other locations were collated by Daisen and others of Aizen-in on this mountain.
I have also made corrections.
Since both versions were printed from woodblocks, [this was done] at the Sōjiji-in under the Myōonrin by Kaidō. Recorded.
First proofread by Cishun.
